stories.headline: Israel kills 2 senior Iranian intelligence officials in targeted Tehran airstrike

key_facts.fact: The IDF confirmed a targeted airstrike killed Abdollah Jalali-Nasab and Amir Shariat, senior intelligence officials of Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Emergency Command, in Tehran on March 15.
key_facts.excerpt: The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) said that two senior Iranian intelligence officials were killed in a targeted airstrike carried out by the Israeli Air Force (IAF) in Tehran.

key_facts.fact: The two officials had been recently appointed as acting replacements after their predecessor Saleh Asadi was killed during Operation Roaring Lion.
key_facts.excerpt: The two senior commanders were key figures in the Iranian intelligence community and close to the leadership of the Iranian terrorist regime... they were recently appointed as acting replacements after their predecessor Saleh Asadi was killed during Operation Roaring Lion.

key_facts.fact: IDF spokesperson Brigadier General Effie Defrin said the strike was part of a broader campaign involving 20 waves of attacks against over 150 Iranian government targets, with hundreds of Israeli Air Force aircraft involved.
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli military spokesperson Brigadier General Effie Defrin stated the strike was part of a broader campaign targeting Iranian military infrastructure... 20 waves of attacks against over 150 Iranian government targets.

stories.headline: Israel destroys late Supreme Leader Khamenei's aircraft at Tehran's Mehrabad airport

key_facts.fact: The Israeli military said on March 16 it destroyed a plane used by Iran's late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei at Tehran's Mehrabad airport overnight.
key_facts.excerpt: The Israeli military said on Monday it had destroyed a plane used by Iran's late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei at Tehran's Mehrabad airport overnight.

key_facts.fact: The IDF said the aircraft had been used by senior Iranian officials and military figures to travel domestically and internationally and coordinate with allied countries.
key_facts.excerpt: The aircraft was used by Ali Khamenei, the supreme leader of the Iranian terror regime, additional senior officials and Iranian military personnel to advance military procurement and to manage coordination with axis countries.

key_facts.fact: Mehrabad is Tehran's oldest airport serving domestic and regional flights, and is a dual-use facility also housing air force assets.
key_facts.excerpt: Mehrabad is one of Tehran's oldest airports, now serving domestic and regional flights. In addition to being the busiest civilian domestic airport, it is a dual-use facility housing air force assets.

stories.headline: Cuba's national power grid collapses amid US oil blockade, 10M without power

key_facts.fact: Cuba's national electric grid collapsed on March 16, leaving around 10 million people without power, as grid operator UNE confirmed while investigating the cause.
key_facts.excerpt: Cuba's national electric grid has collapsed, leaving around 10 million people without power amid a U.S.-imposed oil blockade that has crippled the island's already obsolete generation system.

key_facts.fact: Cuba has received only two small oil import vessels in 2026 — one from Mexico discharging fuel in January and one from Jamaica with cooking gas in February — after Trump cut off Venezuelan oil shipments and threatened tariffs on any country selling oil to Cuba.
key_facts.excerpt: Cuba has received only two small vessels carrying oil imports this year... The first tanker discharged fuel in January at the Havana port coming from Mexico. The second vessel, from Jamaica, discharged liquefied petroleum gas in February.

key_facts.fact: The blackouts sparked a rare violent protest in the communist-run country over the weekend. Cuba entered talks with the US on Friday to try to defuse the crisis.
key_facts.excerpt: The blackouts sparked a rare violent protest in the Communist-run country this weekend... Cuba said on Friday that it has entered into talks with the United States with the hope of defusing the crisis.

key_facts.fact: Trump mused about 'taking Cuba' the same day the grid collapsed, saying 'That's a big honour, taking Cuba in some form,' as he has said Cuba is on the verge of collapse.
key_facts.excerpt: US President Donald Trump mused over whether he would have the 'honor of taking Cuba' on Monday, the same day the communist-run island's electricity grid suffered its first nationwide collapse.

key_facts.fact: The US pressure intensified after capturing Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro — Cuba's most important foreign benefactor — in January 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The United States has ratcheted up pressure this year on long-time foe Cuba since capturing Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, Cuba's most important foreign benefactor, in early January.

stories.headline: IMO: 3,200 ships with 20,000 seafarers trapped west of Hormuz, emergency session called

key_facts.fact: The International Maritime Organization reports approximately 3,200 vessels carrying around 20,000 seafarers are confined west of the Strait of Hormuz due to escalating attacks on merchant ships.
key_facts.excerpt: The International Maritime Organization (IMO) says roughly 3,200 vessels carrying around 20,000 seafarers are currently confined west of the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: The IMO Council Extraordinary Session is scheduled for March 18–19 in London to address the crisis, with Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez calling for de-escalation and greater protection for merchant seafarers.
key_facts.excerpt: IMO Council Extraordinary Session scheduled for March 18–19, 2026 in London... Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez issued statements condemning attacks and calling for 'de-escalation and greater protection for merchant seafarers.'

key_facts.fact: At least 16 commercial vessels have been attacked since the conflict began on February 28, and no more than five ships pass through the strait daily versus a historical average of 138.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 16 commercial vessels have been attacked since February 28... No more than five ships pass through the strait daily (versus historical average of 138).

key_facts.fact: The IMO is working with the International Labour Organization to strengthen seafarer protections and address mental health support and supply provisions for stranded crews.
key_facts.excerpt: The organization is working with the International Labour Organization to strengthen seafarer protections and address mental health support and supply provisions for stranded crews.

key_facts.excerpt: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi explicitly denied ceasefire negotiations, telling CBS News: 'No, we never asked for a ceasefire, and we have never asked even for negotiation.'

key_facts.fact: Total US military deaths have reached 13, with 7 killed by enemy fire and 8 severely injured, after six service members died on March 12 when their KC-135 refueling aircraft crashed over western Iraq.

stories.headline: Brent crude tops $106 as Hormuz coalition efforts stall, IEA calls it historic disruption

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose as much as 3% on Sunday March 16 to top $106 a barrel, with global oil prices having risen more than 40% since the war began on February 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude, the most important benchmark for global prices, rose as much as 3 percent on Sunday to top $106 a barrel... Global oil prices have risen more than 40% since the war began.

key_facts.fact: Trump said he is talking to seven countries about helping secure the Strait, but none of those he named — including China, Japan, France, and the UK — have publicly committed to deploying navies. Japan and Australia both stated they have no plans to send ships.
key_facts.excerpt: None of the countries he appealed to by name – including China, Japan, France and the UK – publicly committing to deploying their navies to secure the strait... Japan and Australia both stated they had no plans to send ships.

key_facts.fact: The International Energy Agency called the Hormuz closure 'the largest disruption to global energy supplies in history.'
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for US-Israel strikes, creating what the International Energy Agency calls 'the largest disruption to global energy supplies in history.'

key_facts.fact: On Monday March 15, oil fell with Brent closing at $100.21 and WTI settling at $93.50 after Trump pressured allies, but prices rebounded by Sunday.
key_facts.excerpt: International benchmark Brent crude futures lost 2.84% to close at $100.21 per barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures fell 5.28% to settle at $93.50.

key_facts.excerpt: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced Sunday that 300 TSA agents have quit their jobs, and the number of TSA agent 'callouts' have doubled from what they were before the shutdown.

key_facts.fact: TSA agents have already missed a partial payment and a full payment. Funding for DHS lapsed in mid-February amid a congressional standoff over Trump's immigration crackdown.
key_facts.excerpt: He said that agents have already missed a partial payment and a full payment... Funding for DHS lapsed in mid-February amid controversy in Congress over President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown.

key_facts.fact: CEOs of major airlines including American, Delta, Southwest, and JetBlue sent a letter to Congress urging restoration of DHS funding and a bipartisan solution to ensure federal aviation workers are paid.
key_facts.excerpt: The CEOs of major airlines, including American, Delta, Southwest and JetBlue urged Congress to restore DHS funding and embrace a bipartisan solution to ensure federal aviation workers are paid during shutdowns.

stories.headline: Zelensky declares Russian spring offensive has failed; France to send SAMP/T NG to Ukraine

key_facts.excerpt: The spring campaign, as it had been planned, drowned in this spring for the Russians; they were unable to advance. They are carrying out offensive actions, but they are all the same – attempts at infiltration and similar tactics. They cannot break through anywhere with equipment – we are burning their equipment.

stories.headline: GEN Pharma gets ethics approval for SUL-238 Phase II trial targeting Parkinson's disease

key_facts.fact: GEN Pharmaceuticals received approval on March 16 from the Netherlands' BEBO Foundation to proceed with a Phase II Proof of Concept trial of SUL-238 targeting mitochondrial dysfunction in Parkinson's patients.
key_facts.excerpt: GEN Pharmaceuticals announced today that it has received approval in the Netherlands from the BEBO Foundation for the Assessment of Ethics of Biomedical Research to proceed with Phase II Proof of Concept Trial for SUL-238 Targeting Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Patients with Parkinson's Disease.

key_facts.fact: The trial, called the SHEPHERD Study, is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study that will use Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (31P-MRS) to assess SUL-238's effects on high energy phosphates in early, untreated Parkinson's patients.
key_facts.excerpt: A Phase 2, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single-Center Study to Assess the effects of SUL-238 on High Energy Phosphates with Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (31P-MRS) in patients with Early, untreated Parkinson's Disease ('SHEPHERD' STUDY).

key_facts.fact: Patient enrollment is planned to start in April 2026 at a clinical site in Groningen, the Netherlands. GEN is Türkiye's leading specialty pharmaceutical company, traded as GENIL.IS.
key_facts.excerpt: GEN can now proceed to activate the clinical site in Groningen, the Netherlands. Patient enrollment is planned to start in April 2026.

sources.title: GEN Receives Ethical Approval to Launch Phase II Clinical Trial for SUL-238 Targeting Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Patients with Parkinson's Disease
